results.location: Test of allergenicity for candidate protein(s)
results.content: Query sequence of PcIMT1 protein exhibited 110 amino acids match with an allergen Solenopsis invicta of 346 amino acids (protein ID: gi 51093373) and the second match was of 137 amino acids with an allergen Cupressus sempervire of 367 amino acids (Protein ID: gi 8101715). Both alignments of PcIMT1 with two allergens indicate a match of only 25.5% (E-value-0.14; Supplementary Fig. S1) and 24.8% (E-value-0.78; Supplementary Fig. S2) respectively, values indicative of non-allergenicity of the protein. [Standing criterion, from Methods: "Online database AllergenOnline Database v15 (January 12, 2015) (http://AllergenOnline.com/) where less than 50% identity with allergenic proteins predicts non-allergenicity".]
results.route_rationale: Percent-identity arithmetic over reported alignment lengths. The denominator convention is never pinned down by the paper, so no faithful formal statement is available; informal inspection is the right tool.

verifier_result.reasoning: The reported percentages cannot be reconstructed from the quantities the paper supplies. Taking the match length over the allergen length gives $110/346 = 31.8\%$ and $137/367 = 37.3\%$, neither of which is the reported $25.5\%$ or $24.8\%$. Under the standard BLAST convention, however, percent identity is identities divided by *alignment length*, and the alignment lengths are not reported, so $25.5\%$ and $24.8\%$ may be perfectly correct figures over an unreported denominator (e.g. $0.255 \times 110 \approx 28$ identities within a 110-residue aligned segment). The phrase "110 amino acids match" is ambiguous between "110 residues were identical" and "the aligned region spans 110 residues", and the two readings give different answers. This is a reporting ambiguity, not a demonstrable arithmetic error, so no flag is raised. Note also that the downstream conclusion is robust: under either reading all four candidate values ($24.8\%$, $25.5\%$, $31.8\%$, $37.3\%$) fall below the paper's stated $50\%$ non-allergenicity threshold, so the non-allergenicity inference survives regardless of which denominator was used.

results.content: In comparison to the untransformed control line, 7PcINO1-line recorded a ~2.61 fold increase in the INO1 transcript under stress as against ~0.5 fold in 10PcIMT1 line and 0.67 fold in 6DC1 line under similar conditions (Fig. 5a,b). PcINO1 specific 37-amino acid gene transcript level expression was maximum in 7PcINO1-lines (~10-fold higher than in 0 mM) over 6DC1 line (~5-fold higher than in 0 mM) (Fig. 5d) while it was absent in 10PcIMT1-line. In case of PcIMT1-transcript an increase of ~1.3- to ~1.4-fold for both 10PcIMT1 and 6DC1-line has been found (Fig. 5f).
results.route_rationale: Fold-change values read off experimental gel densitometry; empirical rather than theorem-like, hence unformalisable.

verifier_result.reasoning: The only quantitative irregularity is terminological: the sentence applies the word "increase" to fold-changes of $\sim 0.5$ and $0.67$, but a fold-change below $1$ is a *decrease* ($0.5$-fold means the level halved). Read strictly, "a ~2.61 fold increase ... as against ~0.5 fold" is self-inconsistent. Read as an elision — "as against a ~0.5-fold *change*" — it is fine, and this reading is corroborated elsewhere in the paper, which states that "Decrease in inositol content was observed under salt stress in almost similar manner in untransformed IR-64 and 10PcIMT1-lines", i.e. the authors do treat 10PcIMT1 as going down. No ratio in the snippet is internally contradictory, and no derivation depends on the wording. This is loose prose, which this verifier is explicitly instructed not to flag.

results.content: Decrease in inositol content was observed under salt stress in almost similar manner in untransformed IR-64 and 10PcIMT1-lines whereas 6DC1 (PcINO1 + PcIMT1) plants exhibited almost no change in inositol pool under salt-stress compared to no-salt condition. However, 7PcINO1-lines maintained an increasing trend of inositol production even under salt-stress. [Fig. 5m tabulated inositol, in umole/gm of tissue: IR64 0 mM = 10, IR64 200 mM = 8; 7PcINO1 0 mM = 55, 7PcINO1 200 mM = 68; 10PcIMT1 0 mM = 15, 10PcIMT1 200 mM = 8; 6DC1 0 mM = 38, 6DC1 200 mM = 38.]
results.route_rationale: Trend claims checked against tabulated experimental measurements; empirical data, not formalisable.

verifier_result.reasoning: Each directional claim matches the tabulated values. IR-64 falls $10 \to 8$ and 10PcIMT1 falls $15 \to 8$, both decreases as stated; 6DC1 is $38 \to 38$, exactly the claimed "almost no change"; 7PcINO1 rises $55 \to 68$, the claimed "increasing trend". The one soft spot is "almost similar manner" for the two decreases, which differ in relative magnitude ($-20\%$ for IR-64 versus $-47\%$ for 10PcIMT1); the phrase is defensible if read as describing convergence to a common endpoint, since both land at $8$. A vague qualitative adverb is not an algebraic or arithmetic error. Caveat on evidence quality: the Fig. 5m values are a transcription of a bar chart recovered during PDF-to-markdown conversion, so they are approximate and unsuitable as the basis of a quantitative accusation.

results.content: Pinitol, detected only in 10PcIMT1 and 6DC1-lines, was found to increase in 10PcIMT1-line, whereas 6DC1-line showed similar increase under 200 mM salt-stress compared to no-salt condition (Fig. 5m). [Fig. 5m tabulated pinitol, in umole/gm of tissue: IR64 0/200 mM = 0/0; 7PcINO1 0/200 mM = 0/0; 10PcIMT1 0 mM = 72, 200 mM = 82; 6DC1 0 mM = 88, 200 mM = 93.]
results.route_rationale: Same as EQUATION::2 — a trend claim over tabulated experimental measurements.

verifier_result.reasoning: The qualitative structure of the claim is confirmed by the table: pinitol is $0$ in both IR-64 and 7PcINO1 at both salt levels ("detected only in 10PcIMT1 and 6DC1-lines"), and both pinitol-bearing lines increase under stress ($72 \to 82$ and $88 \to 93$). The word "similar" overstates the agreement — the increments are $+10$ ($+13.9\%$) versus $+5$ ($+5.7\%$), so the 6DC1 rise is about half the absolute and under half the relative size of the 10PcIMT1 rise. That is imprecise description rather than an arithmetic or algebraic fault, and the direction of every comparison is correct. As with EQUATION::2, the underlying numbers are a converted bar-chart transcription and are approximate.

results.location: Construction of expression vectors with PcINO1 and PcIMT1 genes and generation of salt-tolerant transgenic rice lines
results.content: Homozygous T2 lines showing the presence of hptII gene at 1 kb, PcINO1 gene at 1.5 kb and PcIMT1 gene at 1.1 kb region respectively (Supplementary Fig. S5g-m) were selected for Southern blot analysis of plants from PcINO1-lines (110 plants), PcIMT1-lines (153 plants) and (PcINO1 + PcIMT1) i.e DC1 (98 plants) lines. PcINO1 gene probe highlighted two copies of endogenous INO1 genes in all plants. Southern positive T3 PcINO1-plants exhibiting additional single-copy integration in another locus with specific INO1 probe (Supplementary Fig. S6a-d) were used for segregation analysis (Supplementary Tables S4a-S6a). All the single copied transgenic plants (35 PcINO1-lines, 50 PcIMT1-lines, and 25 DC1-lines) were chosen for further analysis.
results.route_rationale: Plant-count subset arithmetic a careful reader checks by inspection.

verifier_result.reasoning: The selected single-copy sets are consistently subsets of the screened populations: $35 \le 110$ for PcINO1, $50 \le 153$ for PcIMT1 and $25 \le 98$ for DC1, so every selection count is attainable. The copy-number statement is also coherent: two endogenous $INO1$ copies plus one additional transgene integration at a separate locus gives three probe-detected bands for a "single-copy" transgenic, which is the standard reading and involves no contradiction. No arithmetic claim in this snippet fails.

results.content: Data represented average of three plants +/- SD (P <= 0.05). [Repeated, with n = 3, across Fig. 3 ("Data represented average of three plants ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)"), Fig. 4 ("Data represented the average of three plants ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)"), Fig. 5 ("Data represented as average of three replica sets ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)", and again for panels (l) and (m)) and Fig. 6 ("Data represented the average of three plants ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)").]
results.route_rationale: A statistical-notation claim in prose with no crisp formal content; nothing to formalise.

verifier_result.reasoning: The notation is malformed as statistical reporting rather than mathematically false. A standard deviation is a descriptive measure of dispersion and carries no associated $p$-value, so appending "$P \le 0.05$" to a "$\pm$ SD" error bar conflates a descriptive statistic with the outcome of an inferential test. The caption also never names the test, the comparison being tested, the test statistic or the degrees of freedom, and with $n = 3$ the dispersion estimate is weak. None of this is an algebraic, calculus-based or sign-propagation error, and no quantity reported in the paper is shown to be impossible by it — $P \le 0.05$ is a legal probability value, so there is no domain-constraint violation either. Within this verifier's remit the correct answer is therefore no error; the issue is recorded as a reporting weakness in the run summary rather than raised as a finding.

results.location: Comparative Transcriptome analysis by cDNA microarray
results.content: A total of 1252 and 1420 transcripts were up and down-regulated respectively in OsINO1-transformed plants in salt compared to control condition. A total of 1493 and 1403 transcripts were up and down-regulated in PcINO1-transformed plants in salt. However, when differential transcripts from PcINO1-transformed plants were compared with OsINO1-transformed plants in salt, the total numbers of up-regulated transcripts rise to 3183 and down-regulated transcripts were 1607 in number (Fig. 8b). Interestingly, the Venn diagram for overlapping categories shows that on overexpression of PcINO1, salt up-regulates at least 1756 unique transcripts and down-regulates no less than 1093 unique transcripts compared to OsINO1 overexpressor in salt (Fig. 8b).
results.route_rationale: The reported Venn-diagram counts impose genuine finite-set cardinality constraints (a set difference cannot exceed the set it is taken from), which is crisp, non-trivial and fully formalisable.

lean_result.reasoning: I formalised the cardinality constraint that the reported counts must satisfy. Let $U_{Pc}$ be the set of transcripts salt up-regulates in PcINO1-overexpressing plants and $U_{Os}$ the corresponding set for OsINO1; the "unique" transcripts are the set difference $U_{Pc} \setminus U_{Os}$. Lean proved, cleanly and with only the three standard Mathlib axioms, that $|U_{Pc}| = 1493$ forces $|U_{Pc} \setminus U_{Os}| \neq 1756$, since $|A \setminus B| \le |A|$. It also proved the companion statement that the down-regulated figure is attainable: sets with $|D_{Pc}| = 1403$ and $|D_{Pc} \setminus D_{Os}| = 1093$ exist, because $1093 \le 1403$. So the formal result is settled, but it refutes a *reading* rather than the paper. The sentence is ambiguous about which contrast the 1756 figure belongs to. Under the reading just formalised — 1756 unique within the 1493 up-regulated in PcINO1-salt-versus-control — the numbers are impossible. Under the alternative reading, in which "unique" counts within the direct PcINO1-versus-OsINO1-in-salt contrast reported immediately beforehand ($3183$ up, $1607$ down), everything is consistent: $1756 \le 3183$ and $1093 \le 1607$. The second reading is at least as well supported, since the phrase "compared to OsINO1 overexpressor in salt" matches that direct contrast verbatim and the sentence directly follows it, and a three-set Venn diagram in Fig. 8b would naturally report the portion unique to that third comparison. Because a consistent reading exists and is the more natural one, the formalisation of the contradictory reading is not a faithful rendering of the paper's claim, and I do not flag an error. The machine-checked bound is recorded as documentation of the constraint the published figures must respect.

lean.formal_statement:
theorem unique_up_count_impossible
    {T : Type*} [DecidableEq T] (UPc UOs : Finset T)
    (hPc : UPc.card = 1493) :
    (UPc \ UOs).card ≠ 1756 := by
  intro h
  have hle : (UPc \ UOs).card ≤ UPc.card := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.sdiff_subset)
  rw [h, hPc] at hle
  omega

theorem unique_down_count_attainable :
    ∃ (DPc DOs : Finset ℕ), DPc.card = 1403 ∧ (DPc \ DOs).card = 1093 := by
  refine ⟨Finset.range 1403, Finset.range 310, by simp, ?_⟩
  rw [Finset.card_sdiff, Finset.range_inter_range]
  simp

'PaperTranscriptome.unique_up_count_impossible' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
'PaperTranscriptome.unique_down_count_attainable' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

summary:
**Scope.** This is an experimental plant-biology paper (an Author Correction notice attached to Mukherjee et al., *Sci. Rep.* **9**:5358, 2019, on overexpressing *PcINO1* and *PcIMT1* in IR-64 indica rice). It contains **no display equations, no theorems, lemmas or proofs, and no mathematical model** of any kind. The mathematical surface available for verification is therefore very small: 7 snippets, all of them quantitative or statistical assertions embedded in prose or figure captions. Most of the manuscript file (about 1.2 MB of its 1.26 MB) is base64-encoded figure images, which were stripped before extraction.

**What was checked.** Six snippets went to informal review: the allergenicity percent-identity figures, the Fig. 5 transcript fold-changes, the Fig. 5m inositol and pinitol trend claims, the Southern-blot plant counts, and the repeated $\pm$ SD error-bar notation. One snippet — the cDNA-microarray transcript counts — went to Lean, because the reported Venn-diagram figures impose a real finite-set cardinality constraint.

**What Lean settled.** Lean compiled both target statements cleanly, with no `sorry` and only the three standard Mathlib axioms (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`): first, that $|U_{Pc}| = 1493$ forces $|U_{Pc} \setminus U_{Os}| \neq 1756$, since a set difference cannot exceed the set it is taken from; and second, that the down-regulated pair is attainable, since $1093 \le 1403$. This is a machine-checked result, but it does **not** convict the paper. The sentence reporting 1756 unique up-regulated transcripts is ambiguous about which contrast it refers to, and under the more natural reading — "unique" within the direct PcINO1-versus-OsINO1-in-salt comparison reported in the preceding sentence, which has 3183 up-regulated and 1607 down-regulated transcripts — the figures are entirely consistent ($1756 \le 3183$, $1093 \le 1607$). Since a consistent reading exists and is the better-supported one, flagging the claim would have been a false positive, so the Lean bound is recorded as documentation of the constraint the published counts must respect rather than as a finding.

**What could not be settled.** One snippet is `UNVERIFIABLE`: the allergenicity percentages ($25.5\%$ and $24.8\%$) cannot be reconstructed from the quantities given, because the paper reports match lengths (110 and 137 residues) and allergen lengths (346 and 367 residues) but not the alignment lengths that the standard percent-identity denominator uses. Taking match over allergen length would give $31.8\%$ and $37.3\%$ instead. This is a reporting gap, not a demonstrated error, and the downstream inference is robust in any case: all candidate values fall below the paper's stated $50\%$ non-allergenicity threshold.

**Two sub-threshold concerns, recorded here rather than as findings.** (i) The paper describes fold-changes of $\sim 0.5$ and $0.67$ as an "increase", though a fold-change below 1 is a decrease; the paper's own later text treats these lines as decreasing, so this reads as loose wording. (ii) Every quantitative figure caption carries "average of three plants $\pm$ SD ($P \le 0.05$)", which conflates a descriptive dispersion measure with an inferential test result — a standard deviation has no $p$-value — and no test, comparison, statistic or degrees of freedom is ever named, with $n = 3$. This is a genuine statistical-reporting weakness, but it is not a mathematical error and sits outside this skill's remit; a statistical-reporting verifier would be the right instrument for it.

**Verdict.** `NO_ERRORS` at confidence 0.70: every checkable quantitative claim was checked and none failed, and the one formalisable claim came back `PASSED`. The confidence is held at 0.70 rather than higher because the verdict is narrow by construction — it attests only that this paper's handful of arithmetic and counting claims are sound, and says nothing about the biological, experimental or image-integrity claims that carry the paper's actual argument. Note separately that this manuscript is itself flagged "There are amendments to this paper", so a published correction already exists; its content was not part of this mathematical review.

**Lean project.** `MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper` was **reused, not created**, by this run and is deliberately left on disk (`lean_project_kept: true`). The project is shared by many concurrent paper runs — its `Verified/` directory holds several hundred proofs from other papers — so although the Lean queue had length 1, deleting it would have destroyed other runs' work. This overrides the skill's default of letting the final call remove the project, and it is consistent with the skill's own rule that a reused project is not the run's to delete. Per-snippet scratch (`TMP.lean`, `claim.md`) was removed, and the proof was archived to `Paper/Verified/0066-InositolSaltTolerance__MATHEMATICAL_MODEL__0_opus5.lean`.
